items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled corollary at source lines 542-549, original Corollary 11.2.10: a Cauchy sequence of Dedekind reals converges in the classical epsilon-N formulation. The author's proof (source lines 551-562) is short but it consumes three separate inputs and finishes with an explicit estimate: a choice principle converts the pointwise Cauchy condition into a modulus M and a Cauchy approximation xbar (line 552), completeness of the Dedekind reals supplies the limit y (lines 553-554), and the convergence estimate for m >= n is then obtained by inserting x_n and applying the triangle inequality to reach epsilon/4 + epsilon/2 + epsilon/4 = epsilon (lines 554-561). The statement records only the classical formulation; the modulus and the intermediate point are invisible in it.
